materials.note: the building. Rough, near-white, no metalness. Carries all the bounce.
low roughness, the screen-space reflection surface

repetitionSystems.note: pier, arch, triforium panel and clerestory opening all repeat on one 7 m bay pitch
each opening subdivided by mullions on a fixed ratio

proceduralStrategy: Build one bay as a function of the bay pitch, then instance it down the nave; every proportion derives from the bay so the building cannot drift out of scale.
Model the pointed arch as an extruded two-centre profile rather than a half-cylinder — the pointed head is the single silhouette cue that separates gothic from romanesque.
Cut the clerestory openings by placing pier blocks between them rather than by CSG, so the shadow map sees clean geometry and each shaft has a hard edge.
Keep every window a separate emissive plane so bloom and screen-space GI both have a bright source to gather from.
Give the floor the lowest roughness in the scene; it is the only surface that can return a reflection.
